thread:
sarah: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I'm sketching a 'steady->surge' handoff model for dedicated GPU pool autoscaling. Goal: keep a small steady headroom to preserve latency SLOs, then let a short-lived surge path take over for spikes. Thoughts?

leon: +1 on concept. main risk is oscillation if steady headroom is too small and surge keeps flapping nodes in/out.

priya: we should separate responsibilities clearly: predictive scaler manages steady headroom, reactive scaler handles surge admission. operator should only reconcile desired capacity, not make admission decisions.

jamie: agree. also need an explicit circuit-breaker for surge so we don't blow cost budgets. proposal: surge has tokens per-tenant with decay and a shared global cap.

aoife: can we avoid two independent scalers racing? how does the handoff look in the API surface?

sarah: good Q. proposal for API/contract: predictive scaler writes intent = {steady_target, min_ready, prewarm_credit}. reactive scaler can submit transient_intent = {burst_add, expiry_ts, source} which is applied only if steady_target + burst_add <= global_ceiling. operator merges intents (predictive wins steady, reactive wins transient) and emits scale ops.

priya: that keeps a single source of truth in operator. nice. need to ensure idempotency and lease TTLs on transient_intent so expired bursts don't stick.

leon: from implementation POV, reactive scaler should use short-lived leases and a backoff when eviction rate > X. metrics: eviction_rate, node_startup_time_p50/p90, queue_latency.

jamie: sketch of config snippet:
```
autoscaler.handoff: 
  steady_headroom: 6
  steady_batch_size: 2
  surge: 
    token_window_secs: 300
    tenant_tokens: 10
    global_cap: 120
    decay: 0.5
    max_burst_node_add: 30
  circuit_breaker: 
    eviction_threshold: 0.07
    startup_latency_threshold_ms: 2000
```

aoife: love the config idea. question: how do we measure cost impact and roll back automatically if cost SLO breached?

sarah: two mechanisms: 1) cost meter in operator that monitors spend rate and rejects new transient_intent if predicted 24h spend > budget, 2) emergency de-energize flag that disables surge path and relies on steady headroom only. both are toggles on the operator control plane.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary deploy plan created for autoscaler-v2. Stages: 1% tenants -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%, with rollback window 15m per stage.

priya: canary + canary health checks should include both latency SLOs and churn (node add/remove) rate. define thresholds for auto-rollback.

leon: on observability: add a short-lived 'handoff.event' trace whenever transient_intent wins. include tag: source, tenant, tokens_used, steady_headroom_at_time. helps debug races.

jamie: ops runbook notes: if oscillation seen, first knob: increase steady_headroom, second: reduce token_window_secs, third: lower tenant_tokens. document as quick checklist.

aoife: one more: what about tenants that game tokens (small frequent spikes)? do we need a fairness limiter?

priya: yes, per-tenant sliding-window fairness and a short penalty (cooldown) on overuse. keep penalties proportional to cost impact.

sarah: next steps: 1) update RFC with explicit operator intent merge pseudocode, 2) add config schema + validation, 3) implement canary pipeline and observe the three metrics: latency SLO, churn, cost burn. I'll open a follow-up PR with the pseudocode today. :thumbsup:

leon: thanks — will prototype the merge logic and share a branch.

priya: I'll draft the canary health checks and cost guard hooks.
